## T/I/OE suggestions

- order_backlog: classified as I (Inventory) — backlog is in-system WIP.
- production_rate: classified as T (Throughput) — flow across the system boundary (delivery).
- customer_demand: could not confidently classify (none) — exogenous driver; Loom declines to assert.

Reasoning: backlog accumulates inside the boundary; production is the rate of value exchange with the market. Demand is exogenous and carries no T/I/OE claim of its own.

customer_demand.reasoning: Exogenous driver; Loom could not confidently classify it as T, I, or OE.

order_backlog.reasoning: Backlog is in-system WIP — an Inventory/Investment stock.

production_rate.reasoning: Production is the rate of value exchange with the market — Throughput.

d1.reasoning: Demand drives backlog accumulation; supported by both causal and structural tests.

d2.reasoning: Backlog drives production scheduling; causal support present, structural support partial.

d3.reasoning: Production depletes backlog (negative polarity); strongly supported.
